mainTopic: The בן סורר ומורה's procedure, רבי חנינא's rule about a convert whose status changed after sinning, and why the rebellious son is judged by his end.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: every detail of the בן סורר ומורה verse is read strictly because the whole verse is extra. Next, אביי explains that the boy is warned in front of two witnesses and given מלקות by a court of three. רבי אבהו's chain of word-links shows that 'ויסרו' means lashes. The words 'בננו זה' teach two rules: the first judges must be at the second trial, and blind parents are excluded. A new משנה rules that a boy who ran away and grew up before his sentence goes free, but after his sentence he stays חייב. רבי חנינא then rules that a בן נח who cursed ה׳ and converted is פטור, since both his trial and his death penalty changed. The גמרא tests this rule against the משנה and a ברייתא, using the ideas that both must change and that a lighter penalty is included in a harsher one (קלה בחמורה), for the רבנן and for רבי שמעון. The amud ends with a new משנה: the בן סורר ומורה is judged by where his life is heading, followed by a list of things that are good or bad for רשעים and צדיקים.

steps.title: Why every detail of the verse is read closely
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier answer: we learn something from every detail of the בן סורר ומורה verses because the whole verse is extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the entire verse is extra.
steps.whatsHappening: This line ends an answer that started before this section. The גמרא explains why it reads each detail of the verse so precisely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we do not squeeze a limit out of every small word in a verse. Here the whole verse is not needed for its plain meaning, so each detail in it becomes a strict limit on the law of בן סורר ומורה.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the entire thing

phrases.english: Since the entire verse is superfluous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the answer from the earlier discussion of how strictly to read the verses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rule of interpretation: an extra verse is read strictly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe these details are just the normal way of telling the story and should not limit the law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the whole verse is extra, each detail sets a limit on the law.

steps.title: Why does the warning need three people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which says the בן סורר ומורה is warned before three. It asks why, since two witnesses are enough everywhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'He is warned in front of three.' Why do I need three? Two should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and challenges one detail: needing three people for the warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In all of הלכה, two witnesses are enough to establish a fact, including that someone was warned (התראה). So asking for three looks like more than is needed, and the גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: They warn him (from הַתְרָאָה, a formal warning)

phrases.english: And he is warned before three?
Why do I need that?
Two are enough!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question on the next part of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement of three people for the warning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two witnesses are enough for every other matter in the Torah, so three seems unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: warned before two, lashed before three
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה combines two separate things: the warning is in front of two witnesses, and the מלקות is in front of a court of three.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what the משנה means. They warn him in front of two, and they give him lashes in front of three.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by reading the משנה differently. 'Three' refers to the lashes, not to the warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning only needs two witnesses, like everywhere else. The 'three' is a court (בית דין of three), which is needed to give מלקות. So the משנה is describing two different stages.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying (a way of explaining what a text really means)

steps.whatToRemember: Two witnesses for the warning. A court of three for the מלקות.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it is saying:
They warn him before two,
and they flog him before three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to require three people for the warning itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The warning needs two witnesses. The three are a court that gives the מלקות.

steps.title: Where does the Torah say he gets lashes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the Torah writes that a בן סורר ומורה gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is it written that a בן סורר ומורה gets lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source of the מלקות it just mentioned. The next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse only says 'ויסרו אותו' (they will discipline him). It never says 'lashes.' So the גמרא wants a source showing that this discipline means מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Lashes given by a בית דין

phrases.english: Lashes for a stubborn and rebellious son,
where is it written?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַלְקוּת בְּבֵן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה הֵיכָא כְּתִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the מלקות mentioned in אביי's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for giving מלקות to a בן סורר ומורה

steps.title: רבי אבהו's chain of word-links
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רבי אבהו's chain of גזירה שוה links. 'ויסרו' connects to 'בן', and 'בן' connects to 'בִּן', which is a word about lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אבהו said: We learn 'ויסרו' from 'ויסרו', 'ויסרו' from 'בן', and 'בן' from 'בִּן', as in the verse 'If the wicked one deserves (בִּן) lashes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא borrows a teaching of רבי אבהו that links several verses together to show that 'ויסרו' means lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each link passes the meaning one step further. 'ויסרו' by מוציא שם רע is linked to 'ויסרו' by בן סורר ומורה. That verse also has the word 'בן', which is linked by a similar-sounding word to 'בִּן הכות' in the verses about מלקות. So in both places, 'ויסרו' means lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned (here, through a word-link)

steps.confusionAlert: The first 'ויסרו' that we are learning about is from מוציא שם רע, not from בן סורר ומורה. The chain still ends up showing that both of them get lashes.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Abbahu said, for Rabbi Abbahu said:
We learned "and they shall chastise" from "and they shall chastise,"
phrases.notes: The first is by מוציא שם רע (דברים 22:18), and the second is by בן סורר ומורה (דברים 21:18).

phrases.english: "and they shall chastise" from "son,"
and "son [ben]" from "bin":
"And it shall be, if the wicked one deserves to be flogged."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A chain of גזירה שוה links (ויסרו, then בן, then בִּן) shows that 'ויסרו' means מלקות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear example of a chained גזירה שוה, where a meaning passes through several linked words.

steps.title: Isn't 'זה' already used to exclude blind parents?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if he sins again, he is judged by twenty-three. That law comes from 'בננו זה'. The גמרא challenges this, since 'זה' is already used to teach that blind parents are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If he went back and sinned again, he is judged by twenty-three. But isn't this word needed for 'זה', which teaches that blind parents are not included?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and challenges the verse it relies on. That word seems to be used up already.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה learns from 'בננו זה' that the first three judges must also be at the second trial. But elsewhere 'זה' teaches that the parents must be able to point and say 'this one,' so blind parents are excluded. One word should not teach two separate things.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and sinned again
It is needed for (a different teaching)

phrases.english: If he again sinned, he is judged by twenty-three, etc.
But this is needed for:
"This": but not blind people?
phrases.notes: Parents must be able to point and say 'this one.' Blind parents cannot do that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next part of the משנה and challenges its source.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'בננו זה' to require the original three judges at the second trial
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'זה' is already needed to exclude blind parents, so it seems unavailable for another teaching.

steps.title: The extra word teaches both things
steps.stepSummary: The verse could have said 'בננו הוא'. Since it says 'בננו זה' instead, we learn two things from it: blind parents are excluded, and the first judges must be present.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the Torah should have written 'בננו הוא' (he is our son). Why does it say 'בננו זה' (this son of ours)? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the verse's wording carries enough extra meaning for two teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the 'same judges' teaching, 'בננו הוא' would have been enough: 'he is the son you already lashed.' Choosing the pointing word 'זה' adds a second teaching, that the parents must be able to point. So both teachings come from this verse.
steps.whatToRemember: 'בננו זה' teaches two things: the original three judges must be at the second trial, and blind parents cannot have a בן סורר ומורה.

phrases.english: If so, let it write "he is our son."
What is "this son of ours"?
Conclude two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording supports two teachings (שמע מינה תרתי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זה' was used up by the rule about blind parents.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah chose 'זה' instead of 'הוא', so the verse teaches both rules.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the rule about the original judges and the rule about blind parents come from 'בננו זה'.

steps.title: The rebellious son who ran away and then grew up
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a בן סורר ומורה who ran away before sentencing and then became fully grown is פטור. If he was sentenced first, he remains חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ran away before he was sentenced, and then his lower beard grew in, he is exempt. But if he ran away after he was sentenced, and then his lower beard grew in, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives two cases of a בן סורר ומורה who runs away and grows up while he is gone. The timing of the sentence decides whether he is פטור or חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A boy can only become a בן סורר ומורה during a short window of age. Once he is fully grown he leaves that window. If the court had not finished his case before that happened, he goes free. If the sentence was already final, it stays in force.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower beard grew around, meaning he reached full physical maturity

steps.whatToRemember: The cutoff point is the sentence. Before sentencing, growing up frees him. After sentencing, the death penalty stands.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ בָּרַח עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמַר דִּינוֹ,
phrases.english: MISHNA: If he ran away before he was sentenced,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקִּיף זָקָן הַתַּחְתּוֹן – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: and afterward his lower beard grew around, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: The lower beard is the hair that shows he's fully grown, so he can no longer be judged as a בן סורר ומורה.

phrases.english: But if he ran away after he was sentenced,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקִּיף זָקָן הַתַּחְתּוֹן – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and afterward his lower beard grew around, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בָּרַח עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמַר דִּינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of being judged again by twenty-three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Running away and growing up before sentencing gives an exemption. After sentencing, he stays liable.

steps.title: A non-Jew who cursed ה׳ and then converted
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא rules that a בן נח who cursed ה׳ and then converted is פטור, because both his court process and his death penalty have changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says: a descendant of Noah who cursed ה׳'s Name and afterward converted is exempt. Since his trial process changed, his death penalty changed too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related rule from רבי חנינא about a person whose legal status changed after he sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As a בן נח, he would be judged under the court rules for a בן נח and killed by the sword. As a Jew, he would be judged by a Jewish court and killed by stoning. רבי חנינא says that because both his trial process and his death penalty changed, he goes free.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew, bound by the seven מצוות בני נח
'Blessed' ה׳'s Name, a polite way of saying cursed

steps.confusionAlert: Here בֵּירַךְ does not mean he blessed ה׳. It is a polite way to say he cursed.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Chanina says:
A descendant of Noah who blessed the Name
phrases.notes: 'Blessed' is a polite way of saying he cursed ה׳.

phrases.english: and afterward converted is exempt,
since his trial process changed,
his death penalty changed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related rule about a person whose status changes between the sin and the trial.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן נח who cursed ה׳ and then converted is פטור, since his trial process and his death penalty both changed.

steps.title: Trying to prove רבי חנינא's rule from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה's first case supports רבי חנינא. The boy goes free because his status changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה supports him? 'If he ran away before he was sentenced, and afterward his lower beard grew around, he is exempt.' What is the reason? Isn't it because we say: since he changed, his liability changed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use our משנה as a proof for רבי חנינא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases a person sins and his status changes before the trial: the boy grows up, and the non-Jew converts. If the משנה exempts the boy only because his status changed, that same idea would support רבי חנינא's ruling about the convert.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it supports him?

phrases.english: Shall we say that it supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי חנינא, and 'it' is our משנה.

phrases.english: If he ran away before he was sentenced,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקִּיף זָקָן הַתַּחְתּוֹן – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: and afterward his lower beard grew around, he is exempt.
What is the reason?
Isn't it because we say:
since he has changed, his liability has changed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to support step 9 using the משנה in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's rule that a change in status exempts a sinner
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of the boy who ran away and grew up before sentencing

steps.title: The rebellious son case is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. A grown man could not become a בן סורר ומורה even if he did the same acts now, so the משנה's case does not prove רבי חנינא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is different here, because if he did it now, he would not be subject to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the attempted proof by showing that the boy's case has a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grown-up boy is exempt because the whole sin no longer applies to him. If he did the same acts today, he would not be punished. A convert who curses ה׳ today would still be liable, so the convert's case is not like the boy's, and רבי חנינא's rule still needs its own reason.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה does not prove רבי חנינא. The boy is exempt because a grown man can't be a בן סורר ומורה at all. A convert who cursed ה׳ would still be guilty today.

phrases.english: No, it is different here,
for if he did it now,
phrases.notes: 'Now' means after he has grown up.

phrases.english: he would not be subject to death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof attempted in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not reject רבי חנינא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The boy's exemption comes from the sin no longer applying to him at all, not from a general rule that a change in status exempts a person.

steps.title: The משנה's second half: running away after sentencing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second half of the משנה. If the boy ran away after his sentence was final and then grew up, he is still חייב. This seems to go against רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he ran away after his sentence was finalized, and afterward his lower beard grew in, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second half of the same משנה to challenge רבי חנינא. In this case the boy's status changed, yet he is still put to death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא says that when a person's status changes, he goes free. Here the boy grew up and his status changed, yet the משנה says he is חייב. So it looks like a change in status does not free a person.

keyTerms.meaning: His sentence was finalized. The court has already given its verdict.
The lower beard grew around. This is the sign that he is fully grown.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he ran away after his sentence was finalized,
and afterward the lower beard grew around,
he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אִם מִשֶּׁנִּגְמַר דִּינוֹ בָּרַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first half of the משנה failed as a proof for רבי חנינא in step 11. Now the second half is used against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's rule that a change in status frees a person (step 9).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The boy's status changed when he grew up, yet he is still חייב. So a change in status does not cancel the death penalty.

steps.title: A sentenced man is already considered dead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. Once the sentence is final, the person is treated as a dead man, so a later change cannot help him.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are talking about a case where his sentence was already finalized? Once his sentence is finalized, he is a dead man!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חנינא by showing that the משנה's case is different. After the sentence is given, nothing can undo it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא's case is about a change that happens before sentencing. In the משנה, the sentence was already final, so the boy is treated as already dead. His growing up afterward does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: You are saying (are you speaking of...).
A dead man. Someone whose death sentence is final and cannot be changed.

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the person has no legal standing at all. It only means that a change in his status after a final sentence cannot undo the verdict.

phrases.english: You are speaking of where his sentence was finalized?
Once his sentence is finalized, he is a dead man!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the verdict came before the change.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The boy's status changed and he still dies, so status changes don't help.
steps.terutzMaskana: A change after a final verdict cannot help. רבי חנינא's rule is about changes that happen before the verdict.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a בן נח who harmed a Jew and then converted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a בן נח who killed or sinned with a fellow gentile and then converted is פטור. But if he did these things to a Jew and then converted, he is חייב. Why doesn't his change in status free him?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a בן נח who struck his fellow, or had relations with his fellow's wife, and then converted is exempt. If he did this to a Jew and then converted, he is liable. But why? Let us say that since his status changed, his judgment changed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי חנינא again. In the second case, the convert's status changed, yet he is still put to death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the ברייתא fits רבי חנינא, since the convert goes free. The second half is the problem: there was no final verdict here, the status changed, and he is still חייב. So the answer from step 13 does not work for this case.

keyTerms.meaning: But why? It asks for the reason behind a ruling.
Since he has changed (his status changed).

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: בֶּן נֹחַ שֶׁהִכָּה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: Come and hear: A descendant of Noah who struck his fellow,
phrases.notes: Here 'his fellow' means another gentile, and 'struck' means he killed him.

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא עַל אֵשֶׁת חֲבֵירוֹ, וְנִתְגַּיֵּיר – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: or had relations with his fellow's wife, and then converted, is exempt.
If he did so to a Jew and then converted, he is liable.
phrases.notes: He killed a Jew or sinned with a Jew's wife.

phrases.english: But why? Let us say:
since he has changed, his judgment has changed!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בֶּן נֹחַ שֶׁהִכָּה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה's challenge was answered, a new source is brought against רבי חנינא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The convert's status changed before any verdict, yet he stays חייב for harming a Jew. So a change in status should not free him.

steps.title: Both the court process and the death penalty must change
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a person goes free only if both his court process and his type of death penalty change. Here only the court process changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need both his trial and his death to change. Here his trial changed, but his death did not change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חנינא by pointing back to the double condition in his rule. In the ברייתא's case, only one of the two things changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא's rule needs two changes: how he is judged (דינו) and how he is killed (מיתתו). When the convert harmed a Jew, his trial process changed, but his death penalty stayed the same. So he is still חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: His judgment, meaning the way the court tries him.
His death, meaning the type of death penalty.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why רבי חנינא needs both conditions. A change in only one of them is not enough to free the person.

phrases.english: We require his trial and his death penalty to change,
and this one, his trial has changed,
but his death penalty has not changed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the double condition of רבי חנינא's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any change in status should free him.
steps.terutzMaskana: He goes free only if both his trial and his death penalty change. Here the death penalty stayed the same.

steps.title: For אשת איש the death penalty does change
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for murder, which is סייף before and after converting. But for אשת איש, a gentile gets סייף while a Jew gets חנק, so both things changed. Why is he still חייב?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a murderer: before, it was the sword, and now it is the sword. But for a married woman, before it was the sword and now it is strangulation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer from step 15. In the case of אשת איש, the death penalty does change when he converts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a murderer, the sword applies both to a בן נח and to a Jew, so the death penalty didn't change. For relations with a married woman, a בן נח gets סייף but a Jew gets חנק. That is a real change, so the convert should go free by רבי חנינא's rule, yet the ברייתא says he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine (granted) for this case. It sets up a 'but' for a harder case.
A married woman. This refers to the sin of relations with her.

phrases.english: Granted, a murderer,
originally the sword, and now the sword.
But a married woman,
originally the sword, and now strangulation?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רוֹצֵחַ, מֵעִיקָּרָא סַיִיף וְהַשְׁתָּא סַיִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15. The answer works for murder but not for אשת איש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 15 that the death penalty did not change.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For אשת איש, the penalty changes from סייף to חנק. Both the trial and the death penalty changed, so by רבי חנינא's rule he should go free, but the ברייתא says he is חייב.

steps.title: The case is a betrothed young woman, so the penalty stays the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a נערה המאורסה. For her, the penalty is סקילה both before and after converting.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is about a betrothed young woman. Both before and after he converted, the punishment is stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16. It says the ברייתא is talking about a נערה המאורסה, not a regular married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 15 says a person goes free only if both his court process and his type of death changed. For a נערה המאורסה, the punishment is סקילה whether he is a gentile or a Jew. So only his court process changed, and he stays חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed young girl (after אירוסין, before נישואין)
This one and that one, meaning both cases

phrases.english: With a betrothed young woman,
so that both this and that are by stoning.
phrases.notes: "This and that" means before he converted and after he converted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a נערה המאורסה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's case of אשת איש is an ordinary married woman, where the penalty changes from סייף to חנק.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a נערה המאורסה, where the penalty is סקילה both before and after, so only the court changed.

steps.title: The case of the Jew's wife must match the case of the gentile's wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer of step 17. The ברייתא lists the Jewish case right alongside the case of a fellow gentile's wife, so it must be a regular married woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches 'he did so to a Jew' in the same way as 'his fellow's wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. The wording of the ברייתא does not allow us to say the case is a נערה המאורסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא from step 14 places 'his fellow gentile's wife' and 'did so to a Jew' as parallel cases. The gentile case is clearly an ordinary married woman, so the Jewish case should be the same kind of case. That means the penalty really does change from סייף to חנק, and the question of step 16 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of his fellow (here, another gentile)

phrases.english: But "he did so to a Jew"
is taught as similar to his fellow's wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא עָשָׂה כֵּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל דּוּמְיָא דְּאֵשֶׁת חֲבֵירוֹ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the case limitation offered in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 17 that the case is a נערה המאורסה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The parallel wording of the ברייתא shows that both cases involve the same kind of married woman, and that is not a נערה המאורסה.

steps.title: A lighter punishment is included in a harsher one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. If his old penalty was harsher and his new one is lighter, the lighter one is already 'inside' the harsher one, so he still gets the lighter one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the lighter punishment is surely included in the harsher one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the נערה המאורסה answer and gives a new reason why the convert is still חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As a gentile he was חייב סייף. As a Jew he would get חנק. The גמרא here treats סייף as harsher, so the lighter חנק is already included in the harsher סייף he was already liable for, and he is still punished.

keyTerms.meaning: Is surely connected to, is included in

steps.whatToRemember: קלה בחמורה: if the new penalty is lighter than the old one, he still gets the lighter one, because it is included in the harsher one.

phrases.english: Rather,
the lighter one is surely included in the harsher one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 17 with a new principle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A change in the type of death penalty always frees him.
steps.terutzMaskana: A change frees him only if the new penalty is harsher. A lighter penalty is included in the harsher one, so he is still punished.

steps.title: This answer fails according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The קלה בחמורה answer works for the רבנן, who say סייף is harsher. But רבי שמעון says חנק is harsher, so for him the convert's penalty got harsher, and he should go free.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the Rabbis, who say the sword is harsher. But according to רבי שמעון, who says strangulation is harsher, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 19. It says the answer only works according to one side of a known מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, going from סייף to חנק is going from harsher to lighter, so step 19 works. For רבי שמעון, חנק is the harsher one. Then the convert moved from a lighter penalty to a harsher one, and by step 19's own logic he should be פטור, yet the ברייתא says he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for this view)
What is there to say? (the answer seems to fail)

phrases.english: This works well for the Rabbis, who say:
"The sword is harsher,"
but according to רבי שמעון, who says:
"Strangulation is harsher,"
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבָּנַן דְּאָמְרִי סַיִיף חָמוּר אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָמַר חֶנֶק חָמוּר מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle of step 19 by pointing to רבי שמעון's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קלה בחמורה answer of step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי שמעון, חנק is harsher than סייף, so the convert's penalty became harsher. By step 19's logic he should be פטור, which contradicts the ברייתא.
steps.confusionAlert: Be careful: the רבנן and רבי שמעון are not arguing about whether the convert is punished. They are arguing about which death penalty is harsher, and the גמרא is checking whether its answer works for both.

steps.title: רבי שמעון follows תנא דבי מנשה: every gentile death penalty is חנק
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds like תנא דבי מנשה, who says every death penalty for בני נח is חנק. So for אשת איש, the convert's penalty did not get harsher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון agrees with the תנא of the school of מנשה, who says that every death penalty mentioned for non-Jews is only חנק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 20. It explains that רבי שמעון holds a gentile's death penalty is always חנק, so his penalty never got harsher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, the worry was that for רבי שמעון the convert went from סייף, which is lighter, to חנק, which is harsher. But if a בן נח was already liable to חנק, then for אשת איש he goes from חנק to חנק. Nothing got harsher, so he is still punished.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher from the study hall of מנשה

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּתַנָּא דְבֵי מְנַשֶּׁה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon holds like the tanna of the school of Menashe,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: כׇּל מִיתָה הָאֲמוּרָה לִבְנֵי נֹחַ
phrases.english: who says: any death penalty stated for the descendants of Noah
is nothing other than strangulation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּתַנָּא דְבֵי מְנַשֶּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 for רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different underlying opinion that רבי שמעון holds
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי שמעון the convert went from a lighter סייף to a harsher חנק, so he should go free.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון a בן נח was already liable to חנק, so for אשת איש the penalty stays the same and he is punished.

steps.title: That works for the married woman case, but what about the murderer?
steps.stepSummary: The answer fits אשת איש, which is חנק before and after. But a murderer was חנק as a gentile and is סייף as a Jew, so his penalty changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for a married woman: before it was חנק and now it is חנק. But for a murderer, before it was חנק and now it is סייף?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 21. Using the school of מנשה's rule creates a new problem for the murderer case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, murder was the easy case, since it was סייף both before and after converting. Now, according to תנא דבי מנשה, the gentile murderer was liable to חנק. As a Jew he gets סייף, so his penalty has changed.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense (sets up a contrast)

phrases.english: Granted, a married woman:
initially strangulation, and now strangulation.
But a murderer:
initially strangulation, and now the sword?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ, מֵעִיקָּרָא חֶנֶק וְהַשְׁתָּא חֶנֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 21 by applying it to the murder case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of תנא דבי מנשה to explain רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every gentile penalty is חנק, then a murderer's penalty changes from חנק to סייף when he converts, so the problem of a changed penalty comes back.

steps.title: The lighter penalty is included in the harsher one
steps.stepSummary: For רבי שמעון, חנק is harsher than סייף. So the murderer went from harsher to lighter, and the lighter one is included in the harsher one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lighter penalty is included in the harsher one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by using the rule from step 19, now from רבי שמעון's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says חנק is harsher than סייף. So the convert murderer went from harsher (חנק) to lighter (סייף). Just as in step 19, the lighter one is already inside the harsher one, so he still gets סייף.

keyTerms.meaning: The lighter penalty within the harsher one
It is surely included, it surely belongs

steps.confusionAlert: Which penalty counts as 'lighter' depends on who you ask. For the רבנן, סייף is harsher. For רבי שמעון, חנק is harsher. Here we are using רבי שמעון's order.

phrases.english: The lighter one is surely included within the harsher one.
phrases.notes: Same idea as step 19, but here חנק is the harsher one, because that is how רבי שמעון ranks them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the murder-case challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies an earlier principle (lighter within harsher) to the new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A murderer going from חנק to סייף has a changed penalty and should go free.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון סייף is lighter than חנק, so it is included in the harsher penalty, and he is executed.

steps.title: A possible proof: the betrothed girl who sinned and then grew up
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a נערה המאורסה who sinned and then became a בוגרת is judged with חנק, not סקילה. This seems to show that when someone's status changes, the penalty changes. That would be even more true for a convert, who changed completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him: if she sinned and afterward grew up, she is judged with חנק. Why not סקילה? Isn't it because once she changed, her law changed? So all the more here, where he changed completely!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא supports the opinion that a change in status changes the punishment, the view of רבי חנינא, who said the convert goes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נערה המאורסה who sins gets סקילה, while a grown woman (בוגרת) gets חנק. If the girl sinned while young but grew up before trial and gets חנק, that shows her new status decides. A gentile who becomes a Jew changed much more, so his punishment should surely change too.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
She reached full adulthood (became a בוגרת)
Since the status changed, the law changed

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי חנינא, who said that once someone's status changes, the punishment changes too.

phrases.english: If she sinned, and afterward she reached adulthood,
she is sentenced to strangulation.
Why is she not sentenced to stoning?
Is it not because since she changed, her law changed?
And all the more so here, where he changed completely!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having defended רבי חנינא against the ברייתא's challenge (steps 14–23), the גמרא now looks for a source that supports his rule that a change in status changes the outcome.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that once a person's status changes, the punishment changes
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a נערה המאורסה who sinned and then became a בוגרת, judged with חנק

steps.title: רבי יוחנן corrected the wording: she gets stoning
steps.stepSummary: The proof falls apart. רבי יוחנן told the תנא to change the ברייתא so it says she is judged with סקילה. So her penalty does not change after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן told the reciter: say 'she is judged with סקילה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 24 by showing that the ברייתא's wording was corrected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the girl getting חנק. רבי יוחנן said the right wording is סקילה, the penalty she had when she sinned. So the case shows that the penalty stays the same despite the change in status, and the proof is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a reciter who memorized ברייתות for the study hall

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yochanan said to the tanna:
phrases.notes: This תנא isn't a sage of the משנה, just someone whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות.

phrases.english: Teach: "she is sentenced to stoning."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire proof from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof relied on a wording ('חנק') that רבי יוחנן corrected to 'סקילה'.
steps.whatToRemember: The convert discussion ends here. רבי חנינא's rule stands: a בן נח who cursed ה׳ and then converted is פטור, because both his trial and his death penalty changed. The ברייתא's convert who harmed a Jew is still חייב, because his penalty either stayed the same or became lighter (קלה בחמורה), for the רבנן and for רבי שמעון alike. The attempted proof from the נערה who grew up is rejected, because the correct wording is סקילה.

steps.title: The rebellious son is judged by where his life is heading
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a בן סורר ומורה is punished because of what he will become. It is better that he die while still innocent than die guilty. The death of the wicked is good for them and for the world, and the death of the righteous is bad for them and for the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: A stubborn and rebellious son is judged based on his end. Let him die innocent, and not die guilty. The death of the wicked is good for them and good for the world. The death of the righteous is bad for them and bad for the world.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains why the בן סורר ומורה gets such a harsh punishment for what looks like a small sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His actual sin, stealing and eating and drinking too much, is not the main reason for the punishment. The תורה sees where this behavior will lead and stops him before he becomes truly guilty. The משנה backs this up with a general idea: when a wicked person dies, he can no longer sin and the world is spared his harm.

keyTerms.meaning: On account of his end, what he will become

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of נידון על שם סופו is the basic explanation of the whole law of בן סורר ומורה, and the גמרא builds on it next.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A stubborn and rebellious son
is sentenced on account of his end.
Let him die innocent and not die guilty,
for the death of the wicked
is a benefit to them and a benefit to the world.
For the righteous, it is bad for them and bad for the world.
phrases.notes: The word "death" is not repeated here, but it is understood: the death of the righteous is bad.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה נִידּוֹן עַל שֵׁם סוֹפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It does not depend on the convert discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בן סורר ומורה is executed because of the path he is on, so that he dies innocent rather than guilty.

steps.title: Wine and sleep of the wicked versus the righteous
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues the pattern from step 26. Wine and sleep are good for רשעים and for the world, but bad for צדיקים and for the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: When wicked people drink wine or sleep, it is good for them and good for the world. When righteous people drink wine or sleep, it is bad for them and bad for the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps going with the same pattern it used for death. This time it applies the pattern to wine and sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple idea is that a רשע who is asleep or drunk is not out doing harm, so everyone gains, and he sins less himself. A צדיק who is asleep or drunk is not doing his good deeds, so everyone loses, and so does he.

phrases.english: Wine and sleep for the wicked —
are a benefit to them and a benefit to the world,
and for the righteous — they are bad for them and bad for the world.
phrases.notes: Wine and sleep are understood here. The משנה is talking about the same two things, now for the righteous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's pattern from step 26 (death of רשעים versus צדיקים) and applies it to wine and sleep.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine and sleep help רשעים and the world, and they hurt צדיקים and the world.

steps.title: Scattering, gathering, and calm for the wicked and the righteous
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list. Scattering is good for רשעים and bad for צדיקים. Gathering together and calm are bad for רשעים and good for צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When wicked people are scattered apart, it is good for them and for the world. When righteous people are scattered, it is bad for them and for the world. When wicked people gather together, it is bad for them and for the world. When righteous people gather, it is good for them and for the world. When wicked people have calm and quiet, it is bad for them and for the world. When righteous people have calm, it is good for them and for the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes its list with three more pairs. These are scattering, gathering together, and calm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scattering keeps רשעים from pushing each other into sin, so it helps. Scattering צדיקים takes away their joint good influence, so it hurts. Gathering and calm work the other way around: they give רשעים the strength and ease to do harm, while they let צדיקים do good together.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole list shows one idea. Whatever holds back the רשעים is good for them and for the world. Whatever holds back the צדיקים is bad for them and for the world. This ties back to the reason a בן סורר ומורה is punished early: it is better for him to die before he becomes fully wicked.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not expect every item to point the same way. Wine, sleep, and scattering are good for the רשעים. Gathering and calm are bad for them. Read each pair on its own.

phrases.aramaic: פִּיזּוּר לָרְשָׁעִים – הֲנָאָה לָהֶן וַהֲנָאָה לָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: Scattering for the wicked — is a benefit to them and a benefit to the world.
And for the righteous — it is bad for them and bad for the world.

phrases.aramaic: כִּנּוּס לָרְשָׁעִים – רַע לָהֶן וְרַע לָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: Gathering together for the wicked — is bad for them and bad for the world.
And for the righteous — it is a benefit to them and a benefit to the world.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁקֶט לָרְשָׁעִים – רַע לָהֶן וְרַע לָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: Calm for the wicked — is bad for them and bad for the world.
For the righteous — it is a benefit to them and a benefit to the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list from step 27 with three more pairs, and two of them reverse the direction of the pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scattering helps רשעים and hurts צדיקים. Gathering and calm hurt רשעים and help צדיקים.
